newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bond prices closed much higher Thursday after catching up with a broad advance in other debt markets on Wednesday when the Dutch market was closed.
Dealers said professional short-covering accounted for most of the buying, adding that prices may now be poised for a correction after rallying strongly this week.

"Most professionals were short, so we have seen a squeeze up of about one and a half points, but today was probably the last day. We might see 102 the figure (for the June bund future) tomorrow, but then it will be game over," said one dealer.

Some dealers expect Dutch bonds to underperform German bunds slightly in coming months, based on the assumption that the more buoyant Dutch economy will stoke inflation, possibly forcing the Dutch central bank to raise short-term interest rates.
The guilder exchange rate was the key variable to watch, they said, with the central bank unlikely to act on rates unless the guilder started to weaken against the mark again.
In March, the Dutch central bank increased its special advances rate twice in two weeks to support the guilder, but at 2.90 percent it remains 10 basis points below Germany's equivalent repo rate.
